## Freed v26.10.701-dev

Transfer acceptance builds can keep a former Primary as a strict read-only Desktop viewer. Ordinary builds retain the transfer and recovery holds

### Features

- After a verified handoff, a former Primary can adopt the successor with a durable native read-only policy that blocks edits, including automatic read and seen updates, while allowing browsing and inbound sync
- Linux stores Library signing keys in an existing unlocked Secret Service vault and preserves the same identity across app and vault restarts

### Fixes

- Viewer restrictions survive restart, checkpoint replacement and later successor recovery; stale commands cannot sign or enqueue edits
- Transfer previews preserve normal Library startup, and automatic development sample data can be disabled
- Locked or unavailable Linux vaults return an error instead of replacing Library keys
- Desktop Settings shows the ten newest individual releases with complete notes, and descriptions in media-free sidebar tiles are centered
- Compatible native dependency security updates and build-time dependency checks keep release inputs consistent

### Follow-ups

- Primary transfer and consumer recovery remain disabled in ordinary builds. Use the separate signed transfer-acceptance app and a PWA built from the same release source for isolated acceptance
- Installed multi-device acceptance and a verified personal Library handoff remain required; passing synthetic tests does not establish either

### Downloads

**macOS:** `.dmg` (Apple Silicon or Intel, signed + notarized)  
**Windows:** `.exe` (NSIS installer)  
**Linux:** `.AppImage`  

> macOS downloads are signed and notarized for normal Gatekeeper installation.
